texts: bad: the repelling is keyed to the lantern rather than to each burning, so two separate burnings in the same lantern collapse into a single repelling, and "the wintergloss" has nothing to refer back to (a bare mass object introduces no thing for a later definite to pick up), leaving a bare kind name in the repeller slot. Rewrite as: "Whenever a lantern burns some wintergloss, that wintergloss repels nightmoths from the lantern during that burning." - "some wintergloss" gives the substance an identity the second clause can reuse, and "during that burning" ties one repelling to each burning.

bad: "nightmoths" ends up as a bare kind name in the avoider slot, so no actual nightmoth ever avoids anything - the rule states nothing about any individual moth. Rewrite as: "Whenever a lantern burns wintergloss alongside mire-essence, every nightmoth avoids that lantern." - the explicit "every" makes the rule reach individual moths; write "most nightmoths avoid that lantern" instead if you do not mean all of them.
good. the "rarely" hedge is carried on the burning and separately recorded as the quantifier word, with "the Keepers" kept as one named actor.
good. the "sometimes" hedge, the burning's participants and "at the Stilllight Lantern" as the event's location all land correctly, and the named lantern keeps its kind.
